text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia's Supreme Defence Council supports Serbia in resolving problems created over local elections within institutions of the political system.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives managers of Italy's Telecom headed by general manager Tomaso Tommasi. The Italian delegation is discussing possibility of forming partnership with PTT Serbia.

- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic meets U.S. senators Carl Levin and Jack Reed about implementation of the Dayton agreement and directions of Yugoslavia's internal development and foreign policy.
- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia opposed to Croatia's intention to divide the area into two counties, says president of the Serb regional government Vojislav Stanimirovic.
- Yugoslavia's return to the World Trade Organisation should be carried out as soon as possible but measures should be taken to cushion the domestic economy during the process.

- Yugoslavia has two million tonnes of corn for export from the 1996 harvest. However, the world price of the commodity has dropped and the capacity of the country's infrastructure is insufficient to transport that quantity.
- Association of Yugoslav Banks says restrictive monetary policy will be continued this year and money can be issued only if it has cover in hard currency.

- Yugoslav government is continuing the implementation of its policy of peace, the Dayton agreement, renewal of relations with other states, development of a market economy and a democratic country needed for the country's return to the International Monetary Fund, it was said at a news conference.
- Belgrade University rector Dragutin Velickovic remains in his post following a confidence vote and calls for university classes to be resumed.
- Clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army claimed respoonsibility for murders in Kosovo of two ethnic Albanians who supported the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia.
- U.N. Special Human Rights rapporteur for the former Yugoslavia Elisabeth Rehn, who is visiting Kosovo, condemned terrorist attacks in the area.
NASA BORBA
- Protests against annulment of local election results continue. Perseverence is the strongest weapon, say opposition leaders.
- Belgrade mayor Nebojsa Covic, who was recently ousted from the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia, says he would only convene a Belgrade council that was elected by the citizens.
- Plenary session on succession of ex-Yugoslav states to be held in Brussels on January 22 and 23.

- Poll conducted on sample of 2,037 shows 37 percent blame current leadership for the post-electoral crisis, 26 percent believe the crisis can be resolved by recognising results of second election round.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian bakers call for state to provide flour from commodity reserves or they will have to increase bread price.
